title: $Lf^*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the
setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ is bounded constructible
([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Lf^*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]).

proof.text: Put $F=f^*$ on module objects, as in [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], $F$ is additive and exact for every commutative condensed $\Lambda$ and every scheme morphism $f$. In particular this applies without any coefficient finiteness or flatness hypothesis.

source.place: First sentence: exactness, now cited from the existing general exactness node

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a complex $C$ and choose a K-flat resolution $P\to C$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $Lf^*K$ is represented by $F(P)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact functor of step 1. The quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ gives, for every integer $q$, $$H^q(Lf^*K)\simeq H^q(F(P))\simeq F(H^q(P))\simeq f^*H^q(K).$$ Thus the required derived cohomology calculation uses the total derived composite specified in the item.

source.place: First two sentences: compute derived pullback on a resolution and identify its cohomology

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], choose integers $a\le b$ outside which $H^q(K)=0$. The additive exact functor $F$ sends zero to zero, so step 2 gives $H^q(Lf^*K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$.

source.place: Second sentence: the same finite cohomological interval gives boundedness

proof.text: For each $q$, $M=H^q(K)$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Choose the finite stratification of $Y$ given by [def-sfb-constructible-module] for $M$. Its strata are locally closed; $Y$ is of finite type over the field $k$ by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], so its underlying space is Noetherian and every locally closed subset of it is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Thus $M$ is constructible in the sense required as hypothesis by [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback], whose stratifications must have constructible underlying subsets. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback] to $\Lambda,f,M$: it allows every commutative condensed ring and scheme morphism. Its coefficient ring is $p_T^*\Lambda$, its pullback is $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M$, exactly [def-sfb-module-upper-star], and its constructibility is the transported restriction being locally finitely presented on a finite stratification, which implies [def-sfb-constructible-module] after forgetting that the strata are constructible. Therefore $f^*H^q(K)$ is constructible. This existing lemma supplies the stratification, base-changed covering, finite-presentation and coefficient-relabeling arguments of the inherited proof.

source.place: Remaining sentences: preservation of constructibility, factored through the existing general module-pullback lemma

proof.text: Constructibility is invariant under module isomorphism: transport the witnessing presentation on each covering member of each stratum. Using step 2 and step 4, every $H^q(Lf^*K)$ is therefore constructible. Together with the finite interval from step 3, these are exactly the two conditions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Hence $Lf^*K$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Conclusion: assemble boundedness and constructible cohomology
